I have farmed this land a long time, so I do not start from empty. I start from what worked for me before and change only a little. I only have 6.5 mu and 2 people in the house, so I cannot spread myself too thin. Wheat and maize are still my main stomach-and-cash crops, because with well water I can keep the wheat-maize rotation steady. Cotton takes more watching and more spraying, so I will keep less cotton than grain. This year I will put 4.5 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and 2.0 mu into cotton. For seed, I will use the kinds people around me plant when I see they come up well and give stable yield. For fertilizer, I would rather put a bit more than come up short, because if yield falls, that hurts more than a little extra cost. Wheat I will feed a bit heavier on nitrogen for tillering and grain filling, maize I will feed heavier after it gets chest high, and cotton I will split the fertilizer so it does not grow only stalk and leaves. Since I have well irrigation, I will water wheat about three times, maize two times if rain is not enough, and cotton about three times. I will use rotary tillage for wheat and maize because it saves labor, and plough the cotton land once so the soil opens better. I will spray wheat and maize fewer times, but cotton I will watch closer because insects can take it fast. That is how I will keep cost, labor, and yield in balance this year.
